searchText: https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/296 any objections to declaring optional authorize header in the beacon-apis? Should we be defining this as part of the spec itself? Given that, in general, implementations use HTTP rather than HTTPS then using either system would introduce a security risk. fair point, its not 'required' my guess was they watned to run off the ref implementation but haven't asked In the request bodies of the following endpoints: - https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Validator/getAttesterDuties - https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Validator/getSyncCommitteeDuties - https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Validator/getLiveness Except rewards, there are no other endpoints where you can POST a validator public key in the body of the request I don’t mind if we remove the pubkey from the request The other thing we need to tweak is that the response from the attestation rewards endpoint includes an extra redundant list like `data: [{ideal_rewards: .., total_rewards: ..}]` I guess the distinction being the `/validator` endpoints. I'm not fussed either way honestly, but `/beacon` i could imagine calling with a pubkey potentially if you haven't looked it up already, so from a user perspective that may be more useful? It looks like there's currently 2 use-cases, and they're slightly different, but at least consistent within their sphere.. the question is what we do when a third comes along... if we do want to tweak this, can we do it before we do a release? one of the reasons _not_ to accept pubkeys is that the endpoint will only ever return data indexed by validator index, so the client needs to be more careful about returning data in order and without gaps, respecting duplicates, etc. It’s not much harder and we already do this in some other places, but it is a bit annoying yeah, I can PR it first thing monday the outcome of the release discussion was to wait for Capella specs i.e. after Capella on mainnet? personally I think we could release after Capella lands on Goerli its hard to release for 1.3.0 of spec if it hasnt been tagged, so yeh its a tiny risk

excerpts.content:
In the request bodies of the following endpoints:
- https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Validator/getAttesterDuties
- https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Validator/getSyncCommitteeDuties
- https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Validator/getLiveness

excerpts.author: radekkapka
excerpts.content: Except rewards, there are no other endpoints where you can POST a validator public key in the body of the request

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content:
I don’t mind if we remove the pubkey from the request

The other thing we need to tweak is that the response from the attestation rewards endpoint includes an extra redundant list like `data: [{ideal_rewards: .., total_rewards: ..}]`

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content:
I guess the distinction being the `/validator` endpoints. I'm not fussed either way honestly, but `/beacon` i could imagine calling with a pubkey potentially if you haven't looked it up already, so from a user perspective that may be more useful?
It looks like there's currently 2 use-cases, and they're slightly different, but at least consistent within their sphere.. the question is what we do when a third comes along...

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: if we do want to tweak this, can we do it before we do a release?

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: one of the reasons _not_ to accept pubkeys is that the endpoint will only ever return data indexed by validator index, so the client needs to be more careful about returning data in order and without gaps, respecting duplicates, etc. It’s not much harder and we already do this in some other places, but it is a bit annoying
